results.name: disposable PostgreSQL 16 migrated through the journal (incl. 0007) and the API is healthy behind the proxy with no provider configured
two synthetic invoices saved by the operator
operator signs in through the browser
Nudgey offers 'Schedule a follow-up' and shows real counts: 0 Due, 0 Upcoming
the form lists the operator's saved invoices and states the browser time zone
choosing an invoice generates a polite local message (no provider call)
exactly one POST /api/follow-ups (201) and the list now shows 1 Upcoming
the database stores the real UTC instant, the IANA zone, the note and the edited message
the request body carries the UTC instant and zone, never a local wall time or the customer's text in the URL
the item displays its time with the zone
a second active follow-up for the same invoice is refused with a clear message and nothing is added
the invoice page shows the scheduled follow-up with zone, note, message and the 'not sent' statement
rescheduling to the current minute makes the server report it Due (1 Due, 0 Upcoming) and the launcher shows a badge
marking complete removes it from the list, counts return to 0/0, and the row is 'completed' with a timestamp
a second invoice can be scheduled (Vienna Cafe, EUR) and counts come from the database
canceling removes it; the row is 'canceled' with a timestamp
the API process was restarted and the follow-up row is still in PostgreSQL
after restart and reload Nudgey shows the saved follow-up again (1 Upcoming, 11:15 AM GMT+8)
the browser only used auth, invoice-list/detail and follow-up routes: never a parse, PayPal-draft or send route
no request left the page origin (no PayPal, OpenAI, analytics)
no PayPal operation exists, no invoice has a PayPal id, no approval or webhook row
browser storage holds no follow-up data and no console errors or uncaught exceptions occurred
the audit log has the follow-up events with no customer text
